title: Canonical algebraic-space tensor pullback counit on flat-term K-flat complexes
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and f:X→Y a morphism of algebraic spaces over S [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the equivalent small affine étale ringed module models [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. Suppose their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] exist with common localization universe w. Let P be an unbounded complex of Y.SmallModules that is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and whose terms are flat on the small site [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For the fixed smallTensorPullbackComplex f and its total left derived functor [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback], the canonical totalLeftDerivedCounit at P is an isomorphism. There is no condition on K, K', a coefficient map, boundedness or flatness of f.

proof.text: The morphism of algebraic spaces induces the morphism of ringed étale topoi of Tag 03G8. Transport it to the affine small models by the basis equivalences of Tag 039Z. Tensor pullback for this ringed geometric morphism and smallModuleTensorPullback f have the same right adjoint: transport the canonical direct-image functor, whose value on a chart is the compatible-section limit. The adjunction hom bijections give a natural isomorphism of the left adjoints, with the canonical adjunction normalization. Build the ringed inverse-image and scalar-extension presentation on these small sites; its scalar map is pullback of regular functions. The natural isomorphism just obtained identifies the presentation's ordinary pullback with the fixed small-model functor.

Apply the existing general ringed-topos resolving-computation theorem to that presentation, P and its K-flatness and flat terms. It says the counit of the universal left derived pullback is invertible on P. Extend the ordinary natural isomorphism to complexes and localization. The uniqueness of a left derived functor with its counit gives an isomorphism with the recorded totalLeftDerived of smallTensorPullbackComplex f; its defining counit equation identifies the two computation maps up to this isomorphism. Since both the comparison and the presentation's counit at P are invertible, the recorded canonical counit at P is invertible.

theorem smallTensorPullbackComplex_counit_isIso_of_flatKFlat
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} Y.SmallModules]
    (P : CochainComplex Y.SmallModules ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
      (J := Y.smallEtaleModelTopology) (R := Y.smallStructureSheaf) P)
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite
      (J := Y.smallEtaleModelTopology) (R := Y.smallStructureSheaf) (P.X n)) :
    IsIso (((smallTensorPullbackComplex f).totalLeftDerivedCounit DerivedCategory.Q
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso Y.SmallModules (.up ℤ))).app P)
